takeaway: Psoas major joins iliacus to form the iliopsoas tendon, which inserts on the lesser trochanter of the femur, so its main action is flexing the thigh at the hip joint.

question.text: Which one of the following is the main function of the psoas major muscle?

answer.text: Flexes the thigh at the hip joint

lines.text: Meet psoas major, running down from the lumbar spine into the pelvis.
It joins the iliacus, which arises broadly from the inner aspect of the iliac wing.
Together they pass under the inguinal ligament as one strong tendon, the iliopsoas.
That tendon inserts on the lesser trochanter of the femur.
Pulling on the lesser trochanter lifts the thigh forward, like a soldier marching.
lines.say: Pulling on the lesser trochanter lifts the thigh forward, (laugh) like a soldier marching.

lines.text: So its main job is to flex the thigh at the hip joint.
Remember the path: spine, under the ligament, lesser trochanter, hip flexion.
